h: Vayetzei Ois 2 · Torah, Prayer and Yaakov's Sleep at Beit El
The Midrash's Two Openings to Vayetzei

p: "Then you will walk your way securely, etc.;
if you lie down, you will not be afraid" (Mishlei 3:23–24).
as it is written, "And Yaakov went out."
"If you lie down, you will not be afraid" —
"You will lie down and your sleep will be sweet" —
"and he lay down in that place" (Bereishis 28:11).
I lift my eyes to the mountains (heharim)" (Tehillim 121:1) —
to my teachers and to those who formed me.
Eliezer, etc. [came for Rivkah with ten laden camels],
while I [come] without even one nose-ring, etc.
He then retracted and said, etc.:
rather, 'my help is from Hashem, etc.'" (Tehillim 121:2).
To understand the opening to this parashah:
drag him to the study hall;
if he is stone, he dissolves," etc.
the opening of the Midrash Rabbah,
"And Yaakov went out from Beer Sheva
for the sense of the verse hints
that in the interval he hid himself away
in the house of Ever to study Torah;
"Then you will walk your way securely,
and your foot will not stumble."
For Yaakov our father, peace be upon him,
when he went into exile to Charan:
something of the language of deceit had clung to him,
which is the aspect of Esav;
all the more so since he was going
to the house of Lavan, father of the deceivers,
and perhaps he would be soiled with sin there
to go to the study hall of Ever,
"Then you will walk your way securely,
and your foot will not stumble" —
in the manner of what is said,
"lest you strike your foot against a stone" (Tehillim 91:12).

rich.text: — רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן פָּתַח: שִׁיר לַמַּעֲלוֹת אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים, אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הַהוֹרִים לְמַלְפָנַי וְלִמְעַבְּדָנַי. מֵאַיִן יָבוֹא עֶזְרִי, אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהָלַךְ לְהָבִיא אֶת רִבְקָה … וַאֲנִי לֹא נֶזֶם אֶחָד וְלֹא צָמִיד אֶחָד … חָזַר וְאָמַר מָה אֲנָא מוֹבֵד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לֵית אֲנָא מוֹבֵד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי, אֶלָּא עֶזְרִי מֵעִם ה׳: Yaakov looks to his “parents,” his teachers and those who formed him, and asks where his help will come from. Eliezer came with ten camels and he comes empty-handed. Then he takes it back: he will not give up hope in his Creator. The Midrash explains the empty hands: Esav came and took what he had. Rav Tzadok explains this opening in paragraph 8.

which comes in the joining of Chochmah and Binah;
and Da'at is the holy spirit,
as Rashi wrote in [Parshas Ki] Sisa.
And from there is the root
as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote.
And this is what it says:
"By His knowledge the depths were split open."
this is the dew of Atika (the Ancient One);
that is, the shining forth of words of Torah,
in the sense of what is said,
And this corresponds to the three Patriarchs:
as stated in the holy Zohar

p: "Then you will walk your way securely, etc." (Mishlei 3:23).
That is, he will be bound at the root
along the lines of what is written
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, נד עַמּוּד א)
the alef bores through the darkness
and shines to every side, etc.,
That is, Hashem, blessed be He,
will refine him in all the attributes,
as it is written, "He made darkness His hiding place" (Tehillim 18:12).
And on this it is said,
"If you lie down, you will not be afraid,"
along the lines of what is written,
"I will grant peace in the land,
and you will lie down with none to make you afraid" (Vayikra 26:6).
is from the war of the evil inclination,

And this is "you will lie down with none to make you afraid":
free of the turmoil and war of the evil inclination.
"If you lie down, you will not be afraid,"
and [the Midrash] expounded: of Esav and of Lavan;
for the main fear of Yaakov
our father, peace be upon him,
was lest he learn from their deeds;
and the main "leaven in the dough"
enters the heart from their kelipos,
as we have written many times.

h: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman's Opening and the Evening Prayer

p: the opening of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman:
"I lift my eyes to the parents, etc.
and I without even one nose-ring."
At first glance, what does one have to do with the other,
"to the parents — to my teachers," etc.?
For fathers give house and wealth,
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman to teach
over the good of this world;
over the accusation of the evil inclination
against which words of Torah do not avail,
he learned from his teachers Shem and Ever
"and from where will my help come?"
that the evil inclination had not yet been cleared away
to give all his money to Eliphaz,
that his Torah had not availed him
לֹא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם פַּחַד מֵעֵשָׂו
he would have had no fear at all of Esav,
that one depends on the other;
Therefore he was deeply embittered in his soul,
pouring out his speech before Hashem,
and our Sages, of blessed memory, said
that he instituted the evening prayer.
That is: in the great darkness
that may come upon any soul,
עַד שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵצָה בְּעַצְמוֹ
until he has no counsel at all of his own —
he should cast his trust upon Hashem.
To this they alluded in the Midrash Rabbah:
that is, He bears with and has compassion
"You will lie down and your sleep will be sweet,"
as it is said, "And he lay down, etc."
For through this it was revealed to him
that he is attached and bound
when the faculties of mind have withdrawn;

h: Bread of Toil and the Sleep of the Beloved

p: King David, peace be upon him:
"It is vain for you who rise early, etc.,
who eat the bread of toil" (Tehillim 127:2).
That is, at times there is no remedy
even in the study of Torah
"those who eat the bread of toil":
Torah study, which is called bread,
an admixture of the evil inclination,
"that it not grieve me" (I Divrei HaYamim 4:10):
that the evil inclination not overpower me
[and keep me] from reviewing my learning
only one who is the beloved of Hashem,
even at the time of sleep.
was revealed to Yaakov in the dream:
"you will lie down and your sleep will be sweet."
